blocks.content: The Supreme Court shall be a court of record and shall have all the powers of such a court including the power to punish for contempt of itself.

rows: Wilful disobedience to any judgment, decree, direction, order, writ, or breach of undertaking given to a court.
Publication or act that scandalises, lowers court authority, or interferes with judicial proceedings.
Non-compliance with a specific judicial order affecting a party.
Actions undermining public confidence in the administration of justice.
Enforcement of private rights and securing compliance.
Punishment to uphold the dignity and majesty of the court.

items: While Article 129 designates the Supreme Court as a Court of Record, Article 215 confers the same status on High Courts.
Contempt powers of the Supreme Court extend to punishing for contempt of subordinate courts and tribunals across the country.
Under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, limitation for taking actions for contempt is one year from the date of the alleged contempt.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 129 declares the Supreme Court of India to be a Court of Record.
Judgments, proceedings, and acts of the Supreme Court are recorded for perpetual memory and testimony.
The records of a Court of Record have evidentiary value and cannot be questioned when produced before any subordinate court.
The Supreme Court possesses the inherent power to punish for contempt of itself, which includes both civil and criminal contempt.
The power to punish for contempt under Article 129 cannot be abridged or negated even by parliamentary legislation.
